- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33) in recent days, model underestimates; adjust up by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.  
- After a sharp price spike (≥ 5% from prior peak), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +2–4% above peak for next 3–7 days.  
- If model consistently forecasts higher than true outcome over 3–5 days, apply mean reversion: subtract 0.5–1.5% per day from forecast until convergence.  
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-horizon, model often fails to catch momentum; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% per day for next 2–4 days.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome shows strong upward trend (≥ 3% avg daily gain), model often lags; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast for next 5–7 days.  
- If sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67) and price is volatile, model tends to over-smooth; increase forecast volatility by 10–20% for next 3–5 days.
